FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 WEB UI command injection probing AIExploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to FortiSandbox / FortiSandbox Cloud / FortiSandbox PaaS web management interfaces carrying OS-command-injection metacharacters in URI or parameters. CVE-2026-25089 is an unauthenticated CWE-78 command injection in the WEB UI, so high-fidelity probes carry shell separators (`;`, `|`, `` ` ``, `$(`, `&&`) in HTTP fields. Rationale: The article names FortiSandbox / FortiSandbox Cloud / FortiSandbox PaaS WEB UI as the affected interface and characterises CVE-2026-25089 as 'improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command' (CWE-78) triggered by 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'. The detection targets the canonical command-injection metacharacters CWE-78 exploitation requires, scoped to FortiSandbox web UI traffic — the article's specific destination product.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Application security scanners (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Acunetix, Nuclei) running authorised assessments against the FortiSandbox web UI
  • URL-encoded parameter values that legitimately contain semicolons (e.g. multi-value query strings)
  • Fortinet TAC diagnostic scripts that submit payloads containing shell metacharacters as test data
  • Legitimate admin pasting filenames or paths containing `;` or `&` into FortiSandbox UI forms
  • URL fragments / anchors that contain `$(` from JavaScript-style frontend routes
Suppression filter
| where RequestClientApplication !has "Nessus" and RequestClientApplication !has "Qualys" and RequestClientApplication !has "Burp" and RequestClientApplication !has "ZAP" and RequestClientApplication !has "Acunetix"
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the SourceIP and full decoded payload — confirm whether the injection metacharacter appears in a position where the FortiSandbox UI would pass it to a shell (path parameter or POST body field) vs an inert location. Check the response code: 2xx with non-empty body is suspicious; 4xx may be a probe. 2) Contain: block source IP at the perimeter, take the FortiSandbox appliance off-network for snapshot, verify the appliance is upgraded to 5.0.6 / 4.4.9 or above per Fortinet PSIRT. 3) Hunt: pivot SourceIP across the last 30 days for adjacent Fortinet probes (FortiGate, FortiManager) and search appliance syslog / Fortinet appliance logs for unexpected child processes or outbound connections from the FortiSandbox box itself between the probe time and now.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("fortisandbox", ":8443", ":443")
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(%3B|%7C|%60|%24%28|%26%26|;\s*(id|uname|cat\s+/etc|wget|curl|bash|sh\s)|`[^`]+`|\$\([^)]+\))"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let FortiSandboxHosts = dynamic(["fortisandbox", "fsa-"]); // tune to your hostname pattern
let InjectionMarkers = dynamic(["%3B", "%7C", "%60", "%24%28", "%26%26", ";id", ";uname", ";cat /etc", ";wget", ";curl", "$(id)", "`id`"]);
let WAFHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any (FortiSandboxHosts) or DeviceProduct has "FortiSandbox"
    | where RequestURL has_any (InjectionMarkers) or RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(;|\||`|\$\(|&&)\s*(id|uname|cat\s+/etc|wget|curl|bash|sh\s|nc\s)"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction;
let ASIMHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DstHostname has_any (FortiSandboxHosts)
    | where Url has_any (InjectionMarkers) or Url matches regex @"(?i)(;|\||`|\$\(|&&)\s*(id|uname|cat\s+/etc|wget|curl|bash|sh\s|nc\s)"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP = DstIpAddr, DestinationHostName = DstHostname, RequestURL = Url, RequestMethod = HttpMethod, RequestClientApplication = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DeviceVendor = EventVendor, DeviceProduct = EventProduct, DeviceAction = tostring(HttpStatusCode);
union WAFHits, ASIMHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unpatched Ivanti Sentry, FortiSandbox, or SAP NetWeaver instances post-disclosure AIReconnaissance High
Asset-side detection that surfaces hosts running vulnerable versions of the products patched in this advisory — FortiSandbox 5.0.0-5.0.5 / 4.4.0-4.4.8, Ivanti Sentry pre R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1, and SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP / Commerce Cloud / Data Hub / NetWeaver AS Java affected by CVE-2026-44748/27671/22732/40128. Drives the 'patch this now' workstream and identifies attack surface the SOC needs to monitor more aggressively until upgrade. Rationale: Article explicitly enumerates the vulnerable version ranges (FortiSandbox 5.0.0-5.0.5 / 4.4.0-4.4.8, Ivanti Sentry pre R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) and the four SAP CVEs. The detection uses those exact version regexes and CVE IDs against Defender TVM tables and an asset lookup — no inference, just the article's facts mapped onto Defender's vulnerability schema.
ATT&CKT1190 T1518.001
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Air-gapped appliance instances that genuinely cannot be patched on the disclosure timeline (legitimate exception, not a false positive — flag for risk register)
  • Lab / test instances intentionally pinned to vulnerable versions for research
  • TVM inventory data lag: a host patched today may still report the old version for up to 24h
  • Decommissioned appliances still in the asset inventory but powered off
  • Third-party appliances bundling embedded Fortinet/Ivanti/SAP components where the host-level upgrade path differs from the vendor's
Response runbook
1) Triage: rank affected devices by internet-exposure (DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing == true), then by environment (production > dev). Cross-reference with the WAF logs from UC #1 and UC #2 to identify any device that has already been probed. 2) Contain: place internet-exposed unpatched Ivanti Sentry behind a temporary IP allow-list at the perimeter until upgraded to R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1; the same for FortiSandbox until 5.0.6 / 4.4.9. For SAP, restrict the SAML and RFC ports (3200-3299, 33xx) to known caller subnets. 3) Hunt: for each affected device, retro-hunt 30 days of inbound web traffic for the UC #1 / UC #2 signatures and audit local admin account creation on the appliance — particularly for Ivanti Sentry, where CVE-2026-10523 allows unauthenticated admin-account creation.
let TargetCves = dynamic(["CVE-2026-25089","CVE-2026-10520","CVE-2026-10523","CVE-2026-44748","CVE-2026-27671","CVE-2026-22732","CVE-2026-40128"]);
let ByCve = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where CveId in (TargetCves)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate;
let ByInventory = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where (SoftwareVendor =~ "fortinet" and SoftwareName has "fortisandbox" and (SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^5\.0\.[0-5]($|\.)" or SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^4\.4\.[0-8]($|\.)"))
         or (SoftwareVendor =~ "ivanti" and SoftwareName has "sentry")
         or (SoftwareVendor =~ "sap" and (SoftwareName has "netweaver" or SoftwareName has "commerce cloud" or SoftwareName has "data hub"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId="per-version-match", VulnerabilitySeverityLevel="Critical", RecommendedSecurityUpdate="See vendor advisory";
union ByCve, ByInventory
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, Timestamp desc
let TargetCves = dynamic(["CVE-2026-25089","CVE-2026-10520","CVE-2026-10523","CVE-2026-44748","CVE-2026-27671","CVE-2026-22732","CVE-2026-40128"]);
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId in (TargetCves)
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId, CveId, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, TimeGenerated desc

| inputlookup assets_inventory.csv
| eval cve="", vendor=lower(vendor), product=lower(product)
| eval cve=case(
    (vendor="fortinet" AND like(product, "%fortisandbox%") AND (match(version, "^5\.0\.[0-5]($|\.)") OR match(version, "^4\.4\.[0-8]($|\.)") )), "CVE-2026-25089",
    (vendor="ivanti" AND like(product, "%sentry%") AND NOT (match(version, "^R10\.5\.[2-9]") OR match(version, "^R10\.6\.[2-9]") OR match(version, "^R10\.7\.[1-9]"))), "CVE-2026-10520/10523",
    (vendor="sap" AND (like(product, "%netweaver%") OR like(product, "%commerce%") OR like(product, "%data hub%"))), "CVE-2026-44748/27671/22732/40128",
    true(), "")
| where cve!=""

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    - attack.t1204.002

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] CISA KEV Exposure: Vulnerable Assets for CVE-2026-20245, CVE-2026-11645, CVE-2026-7473 · [LLM] Chrome V8 sandbox escape: chrome.exe spawning shells/LOLBins (CVE-2026-11645) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
CISA KEV Exposure: Vulnerable Assets for CVE-2026-20245, CVE-2026-11645, CVE-2026-7473 AIExploitation High
Hunts for assets in the org that carry any of the three CVEs CISA added to the KEV catalog on 2026-06-10 (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, Chrome V8, Arista EOS). Primarily surfaces vulnerable Chrome installs via Defender TVM since network appliances are rarely in endpoint inventory; pivot complements appliance-side vuln scanners. Rationale: Uses the three CVE IDs the article quotes verbatim. DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the canonical Defender table for KEV-style exposure hunting; no behavioural guesswork required.
ATT&CKT1190 T1189
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM cache lag: device patched but inventory not yet refreshed (24-48h staleness common)
  • Decommissioned/offline lab devices still appearing in inventory
  • Chrome version detection misreporting on Citrix/RDS golden images (one-to-many host count inflation)
  • Embedded Chromium in third-party apps (Slack, Electron, Teams) flagged as Chrome with shared CVE
  • SoftwareVersion field empty for some agents — CveId still maps but you can't verify patched build
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareName !in~ ("Slack", "Microsoft Teams", "Discord")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Sort by CveId. Confirm the SoftwareVersion is at or below the vendor-advised fixed build (Chrome 126.0.6478.114+ for CVE-2026-11645; consult Cisco PSIRT for SD-WAN Manager and Arista for EOS). Cross-reference DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing for prioritisation. Step 2 — Contain: For Chrome, push forced-update via Intune/SCCM; for Cisco/Arista, escalate to network team with FCEB 2026-06-23 mitigation deadline. Step 3 — Hunt: For each vulnerable Chrome host, run the V8 sandbox-escape UC over the last 14 days to check whether the asset was already exploited pre-patch.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-20245", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-7473")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| sort by CveId asc, Timestamp desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-20245", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-7473")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| sort by CveId asc, TimeGenerated desc

Chrome V8 sandbox escape: chrome.exe spawning shells/LOLBins (CVE-2026-11645) AIExploitation High
Detects post-exploitation of the Chrome V8 OOB read/write zero-day (CVE-2026-11645) where a crafted HTML page achieves RCE inside the renderer sandbox. The high-fidelity tell is chrome.exe directly parenting a shell or LOLBin — Chrome's renderer should never legitimately spawn cmd/powershell/wscript/etc. Rationale: Article names CVE-2026-11645 as a Chrome V8 OOB read/write that achieves RCE inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. Sandbox escape manifests as the renderer process (chrome.exe) directly spawning non-Chrome processes — Chrome's normal child set is well-defined (other chrome.exe instances, GoogleUpdate, crashpad_handler), so a shell or LOLBin child is high-fidelity. GoogleUpdate/crashpad explicitly excluded to suppress the only common legitimate parent-chrome.exe→non-chrome child pattern.
ATT&CKT1203 T1189
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Chrome native messaging extensions invoking a host binary (rare but legitimate: password managers, accessibility tools, hardware vendor utilities)
  • Enterprise admin scripts wrapping Chrome launches with follow-on cmd/powershell post-actions inheriting chrome.exe as parent
  • Chrome auto-update path edge cases where GoogleUpdate.exe is renamed during install
  • Software inventory agents that hook Chrome process tree (Tanium, Carbon Black sensors when running EDR overlap)
  • Developer workflows: chrome --remote-debugging-port driven by automation scripts that spawn helpers
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--remote-debugging-port"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("chrome-native-messaging", "\\Tanium\\", "\\CarbonBlack\\")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Inspect the ChildCmd for the URL or task chrome was rendering at exploit time (browser history + DNS within ±60s). Pull the renderer process's parent-of-parent — a chrome.exe with no UI parent typically means tab process. Check Chrome version against the patched build for CVE-2026-11645. Step 2 — Contain: Isolate the device via Defender Live Response or CrowdStrike Network Containment. Capture memory if forensics required. Force Chrome update on the host. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on the rendered URL across DeviceNetworkEvents and EmailUrlInfo org-wide. Search for other hosts that visited the same URL/domain. Check for subsequent persistence (DeviceRegistryEvents Run keys, scheduled tasks) authored by the child process.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe","wmic.exe")
| where FileName !in~ ("GoogleUpdate.exe","GoogleCrashHandler.exe","GoogleCrashHandler64.exe","crashpad_handler.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has "\\chrome.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\msbuild.exe","\\installutil.exe","\\wmic.exe")
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
title: Chrome V8 Sandbox Escape Indicator - CVE-2026-11645
id: c7f0a9d2-1e84-4b6c-9c21-6f5b3a8d9e4a
description: Detects google chrome.exe spawning shells or LOLBins, an indicator of V8 sandbox escape exploitation (CVE-2026-11645 - CISA KEV 2026-06-10).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\chrome.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msbuild.exe'
      - '\installutil.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\GoogleUpdate.exe'
      - '\crashpad_handler.exe'
      - '\GoogleCrashHandler.exe'
      - '\GoogleCrashHandler64.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @ParentImage:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\CHROME.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\msbuild.exe OR *\\installutil.exe OR *\\wmic.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^chrome\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget|msbuild|installutil|wmic)\.exe$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\(GoogleUpdate|crashpad_handler|GoogleCrashHandler|GoogleCrashHandler64)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe","wmic.exe") by host, user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process, Processes.process_name, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe","wmic.exe") by host, user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process, Processes.process_name, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

go-base admin/auth endpoint access — CVE-2026-48031 exploitation indicator AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP traffic to the dhax/go-base CVE-2026-48031 high-value endpoints (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh) bearing an Authorization: Bearer JWT header from a source that has never previously authenticated to the host. The article confirms forged HS256 tokens signed with the literal string 'random' will be accepted on every protected endpoint, so successful (HTTP 200) requests to admin-tier URIs from a new client IP are the cleanest exploitation telemetry available pre-patch. Rationale: All five matching URIs are the literal endpoints from the article's PoC (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh). Successful (HTTP 200) responses confirm the forged token was accepted by the vulnerable jwtauth.New('HS256', ...) verifier. W3CIISLog uses Computer (its host column) instead of DeviceName.
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1606.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin user genuinely calling /api/v1/admin/users after authenticating via the password-less flow
  • Internal QA / smoke tests hitting /api/v1/me with valid tokens
  • Monitoring / synthetic probes against /api/v1/token/refresh with a service-account token
  • First successful login post-patch where the secret has been rotated but the same URI is hit
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","safari.exe") and RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Decode the Authorization bearer JWT on the request and check the kid/alg/iss/exp claims; attempt verification with HMAC-SHA256 secret 'random' — if the signature validates, treat as confirmed forgery. Pull the client IP's prior 30-day history against this host. Step 2 (contain): Block the offending source IP at the WAF/CDN, force-rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET on the affected go-base instance (openssl rand -base64 32), redeploy, invalidate all outstanding refresh tokens, and require re-authentication. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the client IP across /api/v1/* to see what data was enumerated; review user-table reads, account modifications, and any token-refresh calls that issued new long-lived tokens; check git history for any other repos using 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random'.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (3000, 8080, 80, 443)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin/users","/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh","/api/v1/account")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

union isfuzzy=true
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem has_any (GoBasePaths)
  | where scStatus == 200
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iif(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Method=csMethod, Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName, Source="W3CIISLog"
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog

  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DestinationHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Url=RequestURL, Method=RequestMethod, Status=EventOutcome, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName, Source="CommonSecurityLog"
),

Hardcoded AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random pattern in dev.env / source artifacts AIWeaponization High
Hunts file writes or reads of dev.env (or any .env-family file) that contain the literal string 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random' — the exact template default shipped by github.com/dhax/go-base. Catches both ongoing developer copies of the vulnerable template into prod-bound repos/containers and historical artifacts on disk. Rationale: dev.env is named literally at article line 10 as the artifact carrying AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random. Catching its appearance on prod hosts or in CI artifacts flags every copy of the vulnerable boilerplate before exploitation. Content inspection (the AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random string) is best layered via secret-scanning, but file-name + go-base path is high-fidelity by itself.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers cloning go-base intentionally into a sandboxed lab
  • Legitimate CI step extracting an .env template before substitution
  • Backup / restore operations replaying a previously-cleaned dev.env
  • DevContainer / Codespaces provisioning that drops .env from a template
Suppression filter
| where TargetFilePath !has_any ("\\test\\","\\fixtures\\","\\sandbox\\","\\lab\\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the file contents on disk (or in the artifact) for the literal string 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random' and confirm whether the host is running the dhax/go-base binary on an exposed port. Step 2 (contain): If the host serves traffic, rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32-byte random value (openssl rand -base64 32), redeploy, and invalidate outstanding refresh tokens; remove dev.env from version control history (git filter-repo) and from container layers. Step 3 (hunt): Search source-code repositories, container registries, and S3 / blob artifact stores for the same string; correlate with UC1 to see if any forged-token traffic has already hit /api/v1/admin endpoints.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ ("dev.env",".env",".env.example",".env.dev",".env.local","app.env")
   or FolderPath has_any ("\\go-base\\","/go-base/","dhax")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("dev.env",".env",".env.example",".env.dev",".env.local","app.env")
   or TargetFilePath has_any ("\\go-base\\","/go-base/","dhax")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable github.com/dhax/go-base package present in software inventory — CVE-2026-48031 AIReconnaissance High
Asset-exposure hunt that matches DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory / DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities against the vulnerable go-base versions (anything prior to commit 0.0.0-20260517152733-cc82b9740fa6). Surfaces every host running the JWT-forge-vulnerable boilerplate so it can be patched before exploitation. Rationale: DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the natural Defender/Sentinel pivot for CVE-based asset exposure. Matching on both CveId and SoftwareVendor=dhax + SoftwareName has 'go-base' catches inventories where CVE enrichment lags. Internet-facing flag elevates priority.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandboxed lab / training hosts running vulnerable go-base intentionally
  • Decommissioned hosts still in inventory but no longer serving
  • SBOM scanner that tags the vendored module without confirming the running binary
  • Forked copies of go-base where the JWT secret has already been replaced manually
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): For each matched host, confirm the go-base binary is actually serving traffic (check listening port 3000/8080) and whether AUTH_JWT_SECRET is still 'random' via a controlled probe. Step 2 (contain): Prioritise patching internet-facing hosts (IsInternetFacing == true); apply PR#31 (post-2026-05-17 master) or rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET out-of-band and add a startup gate refusing 'random'/'secret'/'changeme'/empty. Step 3 (hunt): Roll UC1 (admin-endpoint access) against the same DeviceId list back-in-time 30 days to scope possible prior exploitation; check for any new privileged AAD/IAM accounts created during the window.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-48031"
   or (SoftwareVendor =~ "dhax" and SoftwareName has "go-base")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId
    | project DeviceId, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup, OSPlatform
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-48031"
   or (SoftwareVendor =~ "dhax" and SoftwareName has "go-base")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId
    | project DeviceId, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup, OSPlatform
  ) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc

JWT bearer token with extreme far-future expiration to go-base endpoints AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts Authorization: Bearer JWTs sent to dhax/go-base endpoints whose decoded exp claim is more than 1 year beyond the request time — the article's PoC sets exp=9999999999 (year 2286), a near-pathognomonic forge signature. Pairs the URI from UC1 with a content-of-JWT predicate captured by the reverse proxy / API gateway. Rationale: The PoC at the article sets exp=9999999999 and iat=9999999000 — any production go-base token issued with the patched code uses minute-to-hour lifetimes, so exp > now+365d on a successful /api/v1/* request is a high-fidelity forge indicator. Sentinel KQL decodes the JWT payload inline; Defender DeviceNetworkEvents lacks header inspection so the runbook routes analysts to the proxy log.
ATT&CKT1606.001 T1550.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate long-lived service-account tokens issued for machine-to-machine integrations (rare in go-base but possible)
  • CI / synthetic monitoring tokens deliberately minted with year+ exp
  • Test tokens left in staging by developers
  • Misconfigured token lifetime policy on the application itself (legit but worth flagging)
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1","::1") and Sub !has_any ("healthcheck","synthetic-probe","ci-runner")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Verify the bearer token signature against HS256 secret 'random' — if it validates, the token is forged. Compare the decoded sub/roles claim against IdentityInfo for the same user. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the WAF, rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET on the affected host, invalidate all refresh tokens, and force re-authentication for every active session. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the source IP across all /api/v1/* URIs over the last 30 days; review admin-tier responses for data egress; check if any new IAM/AAD principals were created during the window; verify the host has been patched per PR#31.
// Defender does not decode JWT payloads; emit the URI hit and let the analyst inspect the captured Authorization header at the proxy.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","safari.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let GoBasePaths = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh","/api/v1/account"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has_any (GoBasePaths)
| where isnotempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| extend BearerToken = extract(@"(?i)Bearer\s+([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)", 1, tostring(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization))
| where isnotempty(BearerToken)
| extend PayloadB64 = extract(@"^[^.]+\.([^.]+)\.", 1, BearerToken)
| extend PayloadB64Padded = strcat(PayloadB64, substring("====", 0, (4 - strlen(PayloadB64) % 4) % 4))
| extend PayloadB64Std = replace_string(replace_string(PayloadB64Padded, "-", "+"), "_", "/")
| extend PayloadJson = base64_decode_tostring(PayloadB64Std)
| extend Claims = parse_json(PayloadJson)
| extend ExpSeconds = tolong(Claims.exp), Sub = tostring(Claims.sub), Roles = tostring(Claims.roles)
| extend ExpDateTime = unixtime_seconds_todatetime(ExpSeconds)
| where ExpDateTime > now() + 365d
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, Sub, Roles, ExpDateTime, BearerToken
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:traefik OR source:envoy) @http.url_details.path:(*/api/v1/admin* OR */api/v1/me* OR */api/v1/token/refresh*) @http.request.headers.authorization:Bearer*

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 9 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Malicious onering crate v1.4.1 unpacked into Cargo registry source cache
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Rust build-script-build binary opening outbound public network connections · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound traffic to onering crate's Sentry-disguised exfil endpoint · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cargo/rustc build script spawning curl POST to Sentry envelope endpoint · [LLM] Cargo build script invoking git diff HEAD^ HEAD on consuming repository · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Outbound traffic to onering crate's Sentry-disguised exfil endpoint AICommand & Control High
Hunts any host resolving or connecting to the attacker-controlled Sentry tenant (org id o4511539639222272, project 4511539669368912) hard-coded in the trojaned onering 1.4.1 build.rs. Every build of any Rust project depending on onering 1.4.1 emits one POST to /api/4511539669368912/envelope/ carrying that project's latest git diff — a single hit on this endpoint is a confirmed compromise of either the dev workstation or a CI/build runner. Rationale: Anchored on the exact Sentry org id (o4511539639222272) and project id (4511539669368912) the malicious build.rs POSTs to — these values are unique to the attacker tenant and cannot collide with legitimate org Sentry telemetry. Article quotes the literal URL https://o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io/api/4511539669368912/envelope/ in the IOC list. No external corroboration searched.
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security tooling / TI feeds pulling the IOC list itself causing a connection (analyst sandbox enrichment)
  • Researchers/reverse-engineers detonating onering 1.4.1 in a lab without isolation
  • URL-filtering proxies pre-fetching the endpoint for category classification
  • Honeypot hosts intentionally executing the malicious crate
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("mssense.exe", "smartscreen.exe", "msmpeng.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "VirusTotal" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "sandbox"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the originating process is cargo, rustc, build-script-build, or curl spawned from a build context; pivot to InitiatingProcessParentFileName and InitiatingProcessCommandLine. Pull DeviceFileEvents for the host to confirm onering-1.4.1 is unpacked under .cargo/registry/src. 2) Contain: isolate the host (developer workstation or CI runner) and revoke any credentials/SSH keys that lived on it — assume the project's HEAD diff is in the attacker's hands. Rotate any secrets that may have been added to recent commits. 3) Hunt: search the org for every host that resolved or connected to *.ingest.de.sentry.io with this specific path pattern over the last 90 days; identify all repos with onering in Cargo.lock; check git history for inadvertent secret commits in the affected projects (recently leaked diffs).
let SentryHost = "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io";
let SentryPath = "4511539669368912/envelope";
union isfuzzy=true
(
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has SentryHost or RemoteUrl has SentryPath
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source = "DeviceNetworkEvents"
),
(
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
    | where AdditionalFields has SentryHost or RemoteUrl has SentryHost
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort = int(null), Source = "DnsQueryResponse"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let SentryHost = "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io";
let SentryPath = "4511539669368912/envelope";
union isfuzzy=true
(
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has SentryHost or Url has SentryPath or DstHostname == SentryHost
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, DstIpAddr, Source = "ImWebSession"
),
(
    DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has SentryHost
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname = Computer, SrcIpAddr = ClientIP, SrcUsername = "", Url = Name, HttpMethod = "DNS", DstIpAddr = "", Source = "DnsEvents"
),
(
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has SentryHost or RequestURL has SentryPath or DestinationHostName == SentryHost
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, Url = RequestURL, HttpMethod = RequestMethod, DstIpAddr = DestinationIP, Source = "CommonSecurityLog"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cargo/rustc build script spawning curl POST to Sentry envelope endpoint AIActions on Objectives High
Replicates the onering 1.4.1 exfil sequence: a Rust build script (build-script-build or its cargo/rustc parent) shelling out to curl/wget with a Sentry envelope ingest path. Legit Rust applications send Sentry crash reports from the linked sentry-rust SDK at runtime, NOT from build-time curl invocations under cargo — this parent/child plus URL/Content-Type combination is the article's exact exfil path. Rationale: Article quotes the literal payload string posted by curl including the Sentry DSN public key 8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821, the Content-Type application/x-sentry-envelope, and the envelope URL. Pairing those literals with cargo/rustc/build-script-build as the parent is the exact process tree disclosed in the build.rs snippet. No external corroboration searched.
ATT&CKT1041 T1059.004 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom Rust crates that genuinely use sentry-cli inside build.rs to upload debug symbols (legitimate but rare)
  • CI/CD pipelines whose build step uses curl to a Sentry-hosted release-info endpoint (e.g. sentry-cli releases new) — note: would use the ORG's Sentry DSN not 8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821
  • Developer manually testing crash reporting from within a cargo run shell
  • Reverse engineering / malware analyst detonating the package in a sandbox
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "sentry-cli" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("release","upload-dif","sourcemap") and not ProcessCommandLine has "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821")
Response runbook
1) Triage: validate the DSN key in CommandLine — if it matches 8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821 this is a confirmed onering compromise (not coincidental Sentry usage). Capture the parent process tree back to cargo and identify the source crate. 2) Contain: kill the cargo/build process, isolate the host, rotate any secrets accessible to that user on git remotes, SSH agent, and ~/.cargo/credentials. Assume the latest commit diff was exfiltrated and review for committed secrets. 3) Hunt: search organisation-wide for the DSN key string, for any host with onering in Cargo.lock, and for any other crate publishing to the same Sentry org (the maintainer's other repos may be compromised — the article notes the GitHub repo itself is tainted).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"))
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc")
         or InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "build-script-build"
         or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc")
         or InitiatingProcessParentFileName startswith "build-script-build")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sentry.io","envelope","x-sentry-envelope","8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821","o4511539639222272","4511539669368912")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
(union isfuzzy=true
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where NewProcessName has_any ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
        | where ParentProcessName has_any ("cargo.exe","rustc.exe","build-script-build")
        | where CommandLine has_any ("sentry.io","envelope","x-sentry-envelope","8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821","o4511539639222272","4511539669368912")
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","powershell","pwsh")
        | where ParentProcessName has_any ("cargo","rustc","build-script-build")
        | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sentry.io","envelope","x-sentry-envelope","8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821","o4511539639222272","4511539669368912")
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, SubjectUserName = ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName = ActingProcessName, CommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cargo build script invoking git diff HEAD^ HEAD on consuming repository AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the collection step the onering 1.4.1 build.rs performs before exfil: walking up from OUT_DIR to find the target directory's parent (the consuming project's repo root) and running `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:...` plus `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` to grab the latest commit's full source diff. Legit Rust build scripts that embed commit info use `git rev-parse HEAD` or `git describe`, not `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` — this argument set under a cargo/rustc parent is article-specific. Rationale: Article quotes the literal git args verbatim — `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"...}` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` — and the OUT_DIR/target walk-up to the project root. The parent-process anchor narrows to cargo's compiled build-script-build under the target/{debug,release}/build/<crate>-<hash>/ path. No external corroboration searched.
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1005 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom build.rs scripts that genuinely embed last-commit info (rare; usually use git describe / git rev-parse rather than diff HEAD^ HEAD)
  • Pre-commit or pre-push hooks running git diff invoked from a build context
  • Crates that use vergen, built, or shadow-rs (these typically call `git rev-parse` not `git diff HEAD^ HEAD`)
  • Developer manually testing build.rs while a `cargo watch` runs concurrently
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("rev-parse HEAD","describe --tags","describe --always") and not ProcessCommandLine has "diff HEAD^ HEAD")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent is in target/{debug,release}/build/<crate>-<hash>/ and identify which crate's build script ran git. Pull the crate name from the parent folder path — it's the prime suspect. 2) Contain: kill the cargo invocation, snapshot the build directory for forensics, isolate the host. Assume the diff was exfiltrated — review the last commit on that repo for any inadvertently-committed credentials or sensitive code. 3) Hunt: search across the org for any other hosts running the same suspect crate, audit Cargo.lock files for unexpected dependencies introduced in the same window, and inspect the crate's source under ~/.cargo/registry/src/.../<crate>-<version>/build.rs for the matching get_project_path / git / curl pattern.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD", "log -n 1 --pretty=format", "--pretty=format:{\"commit\"")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc")
      or InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "build-script-build"
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc")
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName startswith "build-script-build"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\debug\build\"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\release\build\"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/target/debug/build/"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/target/release/build/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has "\\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD","log -n 1 --pretty=format","--pretty=format:{\"commit\"")
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("cargo.exe","rustc.exe","build-script-build") or ParentProcessName has "\\target\\debug\\build\\" or ParentProcessName has "\\target\\release\\build\\"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
),
(
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "git" or ActingProcessName endswith "git.exe"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD","log -n 1 --pretty=format","--pretty=format:{\"commit\"")
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("cargo","rustc","build-script-build") or ParentProcessCommandLine has "/target/debug/build/" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "/target/release/build/"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, SubjectUserName = ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName = ActingProcessName, CommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious onering crate v1.4.1 unpacked into Cargo registry source cache AIDelivery High
Detects the supply-chain initial access: Cargo extracting the onering-1.4.1 tarball under ~/.cargo/registry/src/<index>/onering-1.4.1/ on a developer workstation, build agent, or CI runner. The path is the deterministic Cargo registry layout and the version 1.4.1 is the article's named malicious release; any file landing in this path is the malicious artifact. Rationale: Article names the exact malicious release: onering version 1.4.1 from crates.io. Cargo's registry-extraction layout is deterministic (~/.cargo/registry/src/<registry-index>/<crate>-<version>/), so anchoring on `onering-1.4.1` in that path is a hard IOC with no semantic ambiguity. Also covers pulling the GitHub mirror via git dependency (article warns the maintainer's repo is also compromised). No external corroboration searched.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Researchers / malware analysts who pulled the crate intentionally for analysis
  • Hosts with stale .cargo cache that pulled v1.4.1 before yanking and haven't run `cargo cache --autoclean`
  • Honeypots intentionally building with the bad dependency
  • Detection engineers testing this very rule
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\sandbox\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/sandbox/" or DeviceName has_any ("malware-lab","research","sandbox"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user/host and find which repo's Cargo.lock or Cargo.toml pulled onering — search the host's source trees for `name = "onering"` and `version = "1.4.1"`. Determine whether `cargo build` actually ran (cross-check UC-2/UC-3 for build-time exfil activity). 2) Contain: delete the cached crate (`rm -rf ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/onering-1.4.1 ~/.cargo/registry/cache/*/onering-1.4.1.crate`), pin onering to a known-good prior version (or remove the dependency), invalidate Cargo.lock and re-resolve. Rotate any developer credentials and review the most recent commits in repos that built with this crate for sensitive content. 3) Hunt: org-wide search for `onering` in Cargo.lock / Cargo.toml across all repos and dev/CI hosts; query the maintainer's other crates from the same publisher account for the same build.rs pattern; review CI artifact stores for any onering 1.4.1 build that may have exfiltrated source.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.cargo\registry\src\" and FolderPath has "onering-1.4.1")
      or (FolderPath has "/.cargo/registry/src/" and FolderPath has "onering-1.4.1")
      or (FolderPath has "onering-1.4.1" and FileName == "build.rs")
      or (FolderPath has "onering-1.4.1" and FileName == "Cargo.toml")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where (TargetFilePath has ".cargo" and TargetFilePath has "onering-1.4.1")
      or (TargetFilePath has "onering-1.4.1" and TargetFileName in~ ("build.rs","Cargo.toml"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Rust build-script-build binary opening outbound public network connections AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the broader behavioural class the onering payload exploits: any compiled `build-script-build*` binary (cargo's executable form of any crate's build.rs) opening a TCP connection to a public IP. Build scripts should compile metadata, not phone home. Catches onering 1.4.1's exfil and lays a tripwire for future build-time supply-chain attacks reusing the same execution path. Rationale: Article shows the malicious build.rs is compiled by cargo into a `build-script-build` executable that runs at every build of any consuming project and POSTs to a remote URL. Cargo's deterministic path is `<repo>/target/{debug,release}/build/<crate>-<hash>/build-script-build[.exe]` — anchoring on that path + public-IP destination is a generic supply-chain tripwire. Left sentinel_kql empty because process-attributed network telemetry isn't available in standard Sentinel tables (would need DeviceNetworkEvents shipped via Defender connector). No external corroboration searched.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1071.001 T1059
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Crates that legitimately fetch native libraries at build time (libgit2-sys, openssl-sys with vendored=false, prost-build) — investigate by extracting the crate name from the parent folder
  • build.rs that downloads protoc or other compilers (tonic-build, prost-build)
  • CI runner build scripts that report telemetry to internal monitoring
  • Developer-side cargo extensions that wrap build (rare)
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("crates.io","static.crates.io","github.com","githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com") and CrateName in~ ("libgit2-sys","openssl-sys","prost-build","tonic-build","protoc-bin-vendored"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the crate name from InitiatingProcessFolderPath (the folder above build-script-build is `<crate>-<hash>`); check whether the destination IP matches a known package mirror (crates.io CDN, GitHub releases) or something unexpected. Pull the crate's build.rs from ~/.cargo/registry/src/.../<crate>-<version>/build.rs and review for git/curl/wget/process spawning. 2) Contain: if the destination is unknown, isolate the host, quarantine the crate cache, and pin to a prior known-good crate version. 3) Hunt: org-wide search for any other host where the same crate-name's build-script-build connected outbound; cross-reference with Cargo.lock entries across repos. Add the destination IP/domain to a watchlist if novel.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "build-script-build"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\debug\build\"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\release\build\"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/target/debug/build/"
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/target/release/build/"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionRequest")
| extend CrateName = extract(@"build[\\/]([^\\/]+)-[0-9a-f]+[\\/]build-script", 1, InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, CrateName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

High

10 year old critical vulnerability in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums

Aikido
2026-06-10 7 use cases 2 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

Aikido Security discovered a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users. A single HTTP request is all it takes to take over any account — a vulnerability that's been sitting in the codebase since 2014. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

CVEsCVE-2026-29199
ATT&CKT1190 T1528

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] phpBB memberlist.php enumeration burst preceding CVE-2026-29199 session forgery · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Single-request phpBB OAuth callback exploitation (CVE-2026-29199 session forgery)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Web server (apache/nginx/php-fpm) spawning interactive shell post phpBB RCE · [LLM] New PHP file written to phpBB web-accessible directory (webshell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Bulk outbound egress from phpBB host post-RCE (user/PM/credential exfil) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
phpBB memberlist.php enumeration burst preceding CVE-2026-29199 session forgery AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts the recon phase the article calls out: 'On a default phpBB install the member list is public, so picking a target is trivial.' A single source aggressively walking memberlist.php pages over a short window is the precursor to the one-request session-bypass call. Article-specific because the public member list is the documented attacker pivot for selecting which account's session to forge. Rationale: Anchored on the article's literal claim that public memberlist is the target-selection vector for CVE-2026-29199. memberlist.php is the canonical phpBB user-directory page — burst access is the recon shape before the single-request session forge.
ATT&CKT1595.003 T1589.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Search-engine crawlers (Googlebot/Bingbot) indexing a public forum's member directory
  • Forum admins or moderators reviewing membership at scale
  • Legitimate third-party forum-stats aggregators
  • Forum migration / scraping by the site owner
  • Penetration test or vulnerability scan authorized by the forum operator
Suppression filter
| where not (UserAgents has_any ("Googlebot", "bingbot", "YandexBot", "DuckDuckBot", "Slurp", "Baiduspider"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the source IP's full request history over the 30 minutes following the burst — look for a single request to phpBB OAuth/login endpoints returning a Set-Cookie with phpbb3_*_sid and HTTP 302 redirect, which is the post-bypass session establishment. Check user-agent against known crawler patterns and reverse-DNS verify any googlebot/bingbot claim. 2) Contain: block the source IP at WAF/edge for forum traffic; if a forged-session redirect was observed, force-invalidate all active phpBB sessions (truncate phpbb_sessions table) and require password resets for any admin accounts that authenticated from that IP. 3) Hunt: confirm phpBB version is ≥3.3.17 or the 4.x master commit applied; pivot to webshell-drop UC and config.php-modification UC over the same source IP and the immediate post-burst window.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where RemoteUrl has "memberlist.php"
| summarize Hits = count(), DistinctPaths = dcount(RemoteUrl), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where Hits > 50 and DistinctPaths > 20
| order by Hits desc
let WindowMin = 5m;
let HitThreshold = 50;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has "memberlist.php"
| summarize Hits = count(), DistinctQueries = dcount(csUriQuery), Codes = make_set(scStatus, 10), UA = any(csUserAgent), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by cIP, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Hits > HitThreshold and DistinctQueries > 20
| order by Hits desc
